ageing_relevance.rationale: B2M is a GrimAge plasma-protein component and ~10% of its papers concern ageing, but Open Targets lists no age-related disease associations. DNAm surrogate is not measured protein.

evidence.value: One of seven plasma proteins whose DNA-methylation surrogates make up GrimAge, the mortality clock that was +4.3 years older in schizophrenia in part 1 of this project (an effect explained by smoking). The surrogates are methylation estimates, not measured protein levels. Shirai et al. 2024 (7-cohort meta-analysis): DNAm-predicted level higher in schizophrenia/first-episode psychosis.

background_knowledge: Circulating B2M rises with age and has been reported to impair neurogenesis and cognition in mouse heterochronic parabiosis studies; associated with mortality and frailty in cohorts.

mechanism.rationale: The function as an MHC class I light chain is well understood, but the causal link to ageing and the direction of modulation are less clear. Lowering circulating B2M is plausible, but B2M is required for MHC-I.

evidence.value: Component of the class I major histocompatibility complex (MHC). Involved in the presentation of peptide antigens to the immune system.

background_knowledge: Preclinical work suggests systemic B2M is pro-ageing in brain; causality in humans is unproven.

tractability.rationale: There is small-molecule evidence (structure with ligand, high-quality pocket) and antibody evidence because the protein is secreted and on the cell surface. There is also PROTAC evidence, but no approved-drug precedent for this target.

safety.rationale: Open Targets lists no liabilities, but absence of data is not evidence of safety. B2M is essential for MHC-I expression, so inhibition risks immune dysfunction, as in MHC class I deficiency.
background_knowledge: B2M loss causes loss of MHC-I, impaired CD8 T-cell and antigen presentation, and tumour immune escape.

clinical_precedence.rationale: No drugs acting on B2M have reached the clinic according to Open Targets.

assessment.summary: B2M is a secreted MHC-I light chain and one of the plasma proteins behind GrimAge. About 10% of its literature concerns ageing, but Open Targets lists no age-related disease associations. The DNAm surrogate was higher in schizophrenia, but it is not a measured protein level, and the earlier GrimAge difference was explained by smoking. B2M is tractable in principle (small-molecule pocket, antibody-accessible), but there are no clinical drugs. Safety is the main concern: B2M is needed for MHC-I function, so systemic or cellular inhibition is risky. A circulating-pool-selective approach, such as an antibody or clearance, might be feasible. I would rate it 'consider' rather than prioritise.
key_uncertainties: Whether circulating B2M is causal for ageing in humans or only a biomarker
DNAm surrogate is not measured protein level, and the schizophrenia link may be driven by smoking
Whether circulating B2M can be lowered selectively without impairing cellular MHC-I
No clinical drugs or ageing-disease associations in Open Targets
